newsitem.title: UK: Publisher Dorling boosts pre-tax profit by 37 pct.
newsitem.headline: Publisher Dorling boosts pre-tax profit by 37 pct.

text.p: British publisher Dorling Kindersley underlined its status as a growth stock when it announced a 37 percent profit rise on Monday.
A publisher of illustrated reference books and CD-ROMS, Dorling has long been a darling of British share analysts who cite its growth potential in the multi-media age.
Pre-tax profit for the year to June 30 totalled 17.4 million pounds ($27.1 million) against 12.7 million pounds in 1995. The total dividend was increased to 4.5 pence per share from 3.9p.
Dorling shares added 10p to 541.5p on Monday. U.S. software giant Microsoft sold out of the company last November, disposing of a 17.9 percent stake at a price of 507p a share.
Dorling said turnover in the year increased by 25 percent to 174 million pounds.

The company said 77 percent of total turnover came from overseas, with the U.S. being its strongest market. Turnover in the U.S. has doubled in the past two years and totalled 66.6 million pounds last year.
The company's multimedia division grew turnover by 62 percent to 21.2 million pounds.

"Although the U.S. retail environment for multimedia is currently in a state of flux and more challenging than in the past, we believe that a stable market will emerge in due course," said chairman and chief executive Peter Kindersley.
"The directors remain confident of the strength of DK's various businesses," he added. ( $1=.6430 Pound)
